author: Todd Heywood
title: East Lansing stabbing victim's family say they've been 'unrecognized, unacknowledged' - NewsBreak
text:
By Todd Heywood ,
8 hours ago
EAST LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — The family of a man stabbed multiple times just before the police shot and killed his alleged attacker is asking the East Lansing community and leadership to remember “the victim of this attack and the trauma it has inflicted on our family.”
Shelley Davis Boyd stood before the East Lansing City Council Tuesday night to share the gut-wrenching crisis Douglas Mielock and her two children have faced since the April 15 stabbing.
Douglas Mielock. (Courtesy Foster Swift. WLNS) “Much of the public conversation since that night has centered on the man accused of attacking my children’s father and the action of responding officers,” Boyd said. “What has been largely absent and has not been acknowledged is the victim of this attack and the trauma it has inflicted on our family.”
Mielock, 63, is a local attorney. He was employed by Foster Swift and the firm identified him as the stabbing victim of an April 15 incident that led to the shooting death of Isaiah Kirby , 21. Kirby’s family has raised questions about the shooting death and demanded the release of unedited video involving the entire incident that led to the shooting.
Boyd described how her son learned of the attack:
“Our son was on the phone with his father throughout the attack. I want that to sit with this council today. Our son was more than 50 miles away, finishing his junior year in college when he suddenly found himself listening in real time as his father was being ambushed and fought for his life. A brave stranger later picked up his father’s phone and told our son that his dad had been stabbed numerous times. Moments later, our son called me in uncontrollable tears, saying that he could not lose his dad and was racing home from college as fast as he could.”
She said she called her daughter and told her to meet at their home, “because something terrible had happened.”
The two sped to the scene as Mielock was rushed to a local hospital, she said.
At the hospital, her 18-year-old daughter made decisions about her father’s care, Boyd said.
“Although their father survived, survival is not the same as being OK,” Boyd said.
Boyd continued, “What has been especially difficult is watching so much public attention focus on the person accused of this violence while the victim of this brutal and life-threatening attack has gone largely unrecognized and unacknowledged. The loudest voices are not always the ones carrying the deepest wounds. This was not a misunderstanding. This was not an altercation. This was not a mutual confrontation. This was an extreme act of violence.”
She expressed her “condolences to the family suffering unimaginable loss” — the Kirby family — but said the lack of acknowledgement of Mielock was “erasure.”
“I am not here tonight to inflame any division. I am here asking for humanity,” she said. “I’m asking this council, the media and the community to publicly acknowledge the victim of this violent attack and the lasting impact it has had on our family. My children deserve to know that their community sees them and that their father’s suffering is real. And importantly, that victims of violent crimes and their families carrying the aftermath should not disappear from the conversation.”
